source.title: Neuron Coverage-Guided Domain Generalization
source.authors: Chris Xing Tian; Haoliang Li; Xiao-Fei Xie; Yang Liu; Shi-Qi Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains for neuron coverage to improve domain generalization and visualizes selected units, but does not test whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs or measure polysemanticity.
record.gate_note: The paper reports domain-generalization accuracy results, which do not measure polysemanticity. It also reports qualitative visualizations of selected units; those are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, since the units were not identified as polysemantic and the visualizations do not test any listed version.
record.test_reason: A domain-generalization method paper (neuron-coverage maximization). It never mentions polysemanticity, superposition or mixed neuron selectivity, and cites neither original source. Its only neuron-level evidence is qualitative Network Dissection images of two hand-picked ResNet-18 units. These show whether a unit carries a nameable concept, not whether it responds to several unrelated inputs. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that maximizing neuron coverage with gradient-similarity regularization improves generalization to unseen domains. They present the dissection images as support for the idea that inactive neurons triggered by out-of-distribution inputs cause misclassification.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates a domain-generalization training method, not a method for identifying or measuring polysemanticity.
record.method_sensitivity: The layer outputs used for coverage computation changed PACS performance in the layer analysis (Table 7); this analysis did not measure polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: For two hand-picked ResNet-18 units, Network Dissection images show no nameable concept under DeepAll. Under NCDG they show an 'eye' concept (block 3 unit 170) and edges or contours (block 2 unit 20), on target images DeepAll misclassified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron-coverage-maximizing training changes which visual concepts selected units encode on out-of-distribution images (qualitative, selected units).

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The unit-semantic evidence is qualitative and limited to selected units and examples; the paper does not report a polysemanticity rate, systematic scoring, or uncertainty for the visualizations.
record.rows_left_out: Domain-generalization accuracy tables and parameter analyses are not rows because they do not measure neuron polysemanticity or the listed versions.

untested.parts: Whether vision-classifier neurons respond to several unrelated inputs; not examined.
Superposition or capacity as the cause; not studied.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization or noise; not studied.
Effect of activation function or regularization on polysemanticity. The PReLU/ELU and L1 comparisons measure accuracy only.
Reinterpretation of polysemantic neurons as one shared feature; not studied.
Dependence on activation range or explanation scoring; not studied.

record.verdict_notes: No relation value fits exactly: the paper neither cites nor discusses polysemantic neurons. 'cites_only' is used as the closest weak-relation category in place of the record's 'discusses', which overstates the link. All rows correctly carry ['none']. They are best read as context, not evidence on the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Whether image-classifier neurons respond strongly to several unrelated inputs.
Language-model neurons, token or context polysemanticity, and layer differences in its prevalence.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Whether architecture, activation function, or regularization changes polysemanticity or its performance tradeoff.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons have a shared feature or related jobs, and how common unrelated mixtures are.
Whether polysemanticity depends on activation range examined or explanation-scoring method.

rows.subject: DeepAll Resnet-18
rows.operation_detail: Visualized block 3 unit 170 using network dissection.

conditions.value: two person-category images from each target domain, misclassified by DeepAll

rows.measure: Qualitative visualized unit activation and semantic information
rows.value: The selected unit was not activated when trained with DeepAll; the authors report no semantic information in its visualizations.
rows.note: The text describes the visualization outcome; this is not a test of polysemanticity.
rows.check: The value conflates two facts. The text says unit 170 is not activated when DeepAll is trained on Sketch, yet all shown target-domain test images do activate it, with no semantic content visible. Also a comparison of the study's own method against a baseline, not a polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: NCDG Resnet-18
rows.operation_detail: Visualized block 3 unit 170 using network dissection.

conditions.value: two person-category images from each target domain, correctly predicted by NCDG

rows.measure: Qualitative visualized unit activation and semantic information
rows.value: All shown test samples activated unit 170; the authors report that the concept of an eye was consistently extracted.
rows.note: This is a qualitative finding for a selected unit, not evidence about the prevalence or frequency of polysemanticity.
rows.check: numbers_found '1/1' does not appear in the text; it should be empty. The row reports the study's own method on images it selected, not a polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: DeepAll Resnet-18
rows.operation_detail: Visualized block 2 unit 20 using network dissection.
rows.measure: Qualitative visualized unit activation and semantic information
rows.value: The authors report that they could not observe useful information extracted by this unit in the DeepAll baseline.
rows.note: The text describes the visualization outcome; it does not establish whether the unit responds to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: Comparison of the study's own method against a baseline; a qualitative 'no useful information' remark, not a selectivity or polysemanticity measure.
